build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not module 2: its packed bytes end at $CDA5 (934 bytes, the same on sides 2, 3 and 4); the unpacker reads on to the end of its four-sector window, so on side 2 these are the sector's filler (90 00 00 01 00 DC 05 00 repeated) decoded with module 2's table. Nothing reads them

comments.text: Location module 2, the library, where skills are learned for skill points. The game runs it for a square whose action record (at $5F/$60) starts with $82 (game $8845: JSR $03BF with A = 2, then JSR $CA00). Keeps the picture state $AB/$AC on the stack, copies the library's name, record bytes 4-15, to the location name at $F4D0 and shows picture 2 from the buffer at $E000 ($041C). The loop at $CA1A: roster shown, the greeting (the map message record byte 3 names, print_map_message), 'Who wants to enter?' (pick_member, asked even in a party of one); a member who is not conscious is 'in no condition to learn'. Otherwise the member's roster line is highlighted, the text window opened and the loop at $CA59 runs: no skill points (+$20): 'You have too much on your mind to learn anything.'; no empty skill pair among the 30: 'Not even Einstein can learn anymore.'; nothing on offer that the member's IQ allows (count_offered_skills): '... is not smart enough to learn anything here.'; else the list (header '   IQ PTS LVL   SKILL', one skill_list_line per skill), the skill points and list_choose. A skill chosen (record byte $0F + item): its base cost must not exceed the points (unsigned, $CAA5), else 'Not enough skill points!'. A skill the member lacks goes into the first empty pair at level 1 for the base cost ($CB1C). One the member has: level 255 'You know it all.', a level not below the rank (+$24) 'Need more experience.'; otherwise the cost is base x 2^level (level_cost, 255 when larger) and the points left are tested with SBC/BMI ($CB03): a remainder of 128 or more is refused, and a cost more than 128 above the points wraps to a small positive remainder that becomes the new points (cost 255 adds one point, 192 adds 64). Each success flashes the line, and the list returns while points remain. Left-arrow at the member question leaves: $AB/$AC put back, the map stream the picture overwrote unpacked again ($03C5), carry set, so the game redraws ($8872 -> $AC8C). It never saves the game.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $CA4B, written at $CA30: the party position (1-7) picked at 'Who wants to enter?', whose roster line is highlighted ($02C9) before the member's training starts; the code after it is the library's training loop (see library).

The record offset (+$80 to +$BA) of the skill pair being trained: the pair holding the skill ($CAE4) or the first empty one ($CB1C), from find_skill_pair. At $CB31 it is reused for the base cost of a new skill before that is taken from the skill points.
The cost of the skill's next level, base x 2^level from level_cost (255 when larger), stored at $CAFC and subtracted from the skill points at $CB04.

Sets up the library's list: $47/$48 = skill_list_line; walks the record's skill numbers from byte $10 to the $FF that ends them: $4D = 1 + the number of skills on offer (the list's items run from 1 to $4D-1), $4E = 1 + the number whose minimum IQ (skill_min_iq) is at most the member's IQ (+$0F), and $D1 = the last of those, the line list_line_label marks with '_' instead of '>'.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $CB7E, written at $CB5F: the offset in the library's map record of the skill number count_offered_skills is looking at, from $10 on.

Prints 'Skill points = ' (message 4, direct; its {03} clears the rest of the line) and A, the member's skill points (+$20), at column 14, row 2, above the list. Its $30 = 2 changes nothing: print_byte sets $30 to 8 itself ($1CA9).

Per-item routine of the library's list: list_show_page calls it through $47/$48 with A = an item from 1, whose skill is record byte $0F + A (offered_skill). Declines (carry set, $CBF5) a skill whose minimum IQ is above the member's IQ (+$0F). Otherwise list_line_label, then the minimum IQ in two columns, the cost of the member's next level in three (level_cost with X = level + 1: the base cost for a skill not yet known), the member's level in three (skill_level $0359, 0 when the skill is absent), and the skill's name: engine message n, with $43/$44 loaded from the word at $0200, which holds the engine's text block address $29E4; carry clear.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $CBAC, written at $CB98: the skill skill_list_line is printing; LDA $CBAD reads it again at $CBC4 (for skill_level) and $CBED (for the name).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $CBCF, written at $CBC1: the base cost of the skill on the line, handed to level_cost.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $CBDC, written at $CBCA: the member's level in the skill on the line, printed in the LVL column.

Cost of a skill level: A = base cost (1-3), X = level + 1; returns A = base x 2^level, or $FF (255) when that passes 255 (the doubling at $CBFD or the adding at $CC0E carries out; the PLA at $CC16 drops the base cost the early exit leaves on the stack). The doubling leaves 2^level in level_cost_mult_op, which the adding loop reads back. Called for the PTS column ($CBD1) and before raising a skill the member has ($CAF9).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $CC07, written at $CC02: 2^level, the multiplier; the ADC at $CC0E reads the same byte to add it once more per unit of base cost.

Looks for skill A among the member's 30 skill pairs (number, level) at +$80 to +$BB: carry clear with Y = the offset of the pair's number byte when found, carry set when not. A = 0 finds the first empty pair.
Points $16/$17 at skill A's byte in skill_requirements, $CC6C + A.
A = the base cost of the skill whose skill_requirements byte is at ($16): bits 0-2, 1 to 3 for the skills the libraries offer.
A = the minimum IQ of the skill whose skill_requirements byte is at ($16): bits 3-7, 3 to 24 for the skills the libraries offer.
A = the skill on item A of the library's list: byte $0F + A of the library's map record, so item 1 is record byte $10.
Prints message A of the library's text block with direct output (output_direct $02FF), each character drawn at once; then as library_print_wrapped from $CC57.
Prints message A of the library's text block word-wrapped (output_wrapped $0302): at $CC57 it points $43/$44 at the block, $CC90, and jumps to print_message ($0311).

Puts the text cursor at column 14, row 2, the first line inside the text window. Called before the list header (message 3, which opens with a newline, so its text lands on row 3), by show_skill_points ('Skill points =' on row 2) and before the refusals (messages 7, 8 and 10), which print over that line.

Requirements of skills 0-35, one byte each, indexed by skill number (skill_table_entry): bits 3-7 the minimum IQ, bits 0-2 the base cost of level 1. Skills 1-7 $19 (IQ 3, cost 1), 8-9 $31 (6, 1), 10-12 $49 (9, 1), 13-16 $51 (10, 1), 17 Combat shooting $FF (31, 7; no library's record offers it), 18 $59 (11, 1), 19 $61 (12, 1), 20-21 $69 (13, 1), 22-23 $71 (14, 1), 24-26 $7A (15, 2), 27 $82 (16, 2), 28 $8A (17, 2), 29 $9B (19, 3), 30-31 $A3 (20, 3), 32 $AB (21, 3), 33 $B3 (22, 3), 34 $BB (23, 3), 35 $C3 (24, 3). Entry 0, $09, belongs to no skill a library offers.

The library's packed text block (the engine's format; library_print_wrapped points $43/$44 here). These 60 bytes are its alphabet: entries $00-$21 are ' ', n, o, e, t, i, l, a, s, r, the end code ($00, code $0A), h, newline, y, u, '.', m, p, k, g, c, {06}, {03}, w, v, d, {07}, {0B}, x, q, '?', '=', '!', {08}; codes $00-$1D give entries $00-$1D, the escape code $1F followed by 0-3 gives entries $1E-$21, and code $1E is the capital shift; $22-$3B are unused $7F.

The library text's group table: offsets from $CCCC to the groups of four messages, +$08 = $CCD4 (messages 0-3), +$5C = $CD28 (4-7), +$9F = $CD6B (8-11). The fourth word, $74A6 at $CCD2, would point outside the block; nothing asks for messages 12-15.

Library messages 0-3, one bit stream: 0 empty (never printed); 1 '{07}You have too much on your mind to learn anything.
{06}' (no skill points, $CA5F); 2 '{07}Not even Einstein can learn anymore.
{06}' (no empty skill pair, $CA6E); 3 '
   IQ PTS LVL   SKILL
', the list header ($CA82). {07} opens the text window, {06} waits at '(RETURN)'.

Library messages 4-7: 4 'Skill points = {03}{08}' (show_skill_points); 5 'Who wants to enter?
' ($CA24); 6 '
{0B} is in no condition to learn.
{06}' (the member is not conscious, $CA38; {0B} is the name); 7 'Not enough skill points!{03}' ($CAAD).

Library messages 8-10, the last it prints: 8 'You know it all.{03}' (level 255, $CAC8); 9 '{07}{0B} is not smart enough to learn anything here.\n{06}' (no skill on offer within the member's IQ, $CAC0); 10 'Need more experience.{03}' (level not below the rank, $CACC). Message 10's end code is in $CDA4.

The last byte module 2's own packed data decodes to ($D0): its 847 packed bytes, the same on sides 2, 3 and 4, give $CA00-$CDA5, 934 bytes. It follows message 10's end code ($CDA4) and nothing reads it: the library prints messages 1-10 only, and no instruction or pointer in the module reaches past $CDA4.

$CDA6-$CF3E: not module 2. The unpacker decodes a 4-page read window ($CE), not the stream's length, and on side 2 (this snapshot) module 2's 847 packed bytes end at byte $9A of T33/L3. The window reads on through the rest of that sector, 101 bytes equal to the last 101 of side 2's item table (entry 2 of T35/L15, T33/L16-L14: item 82's bytes 3-7, then items 83-94, of which 83, 84 and 85 are alike, DC 05 00 90 00 00 01 00), which give $CDA6-$CEEF, and the first 76 bytes of T33/L2, where tile set 2's stream begins, which give $CEF0-$CF3E; all are decoded here with module 2's table. Nothing reads them.
